title: Choosing statistical representations
summary: Choose a statistical display by matching its purpose, data type, audience and required detail.
objectives: Compare the strengths and limits of dot diagrams, histograms, stem-and-leaf diagrams and tables.
Select a representation for discrete or continuous data.
Justify a choice using the information it preserves or hides.

blocks.text: A useful representation answers the intended question. Dot plots reveal individual repeats and gaps in small datasets. Stem-and-leaf diagrams retain exact ordered values. Histograms reveal the shape of a grouped continuous distribution. Frequency tables support compact lookup and calculation.

sections.title: Account for scale and sample size

blocks.text: A display that works for 20 observations may fail for 2,000. Dot plots and stem-and-leaf diagrams can become crowded, while grouping makes a histogram scalable but sacrifices exact individual values. Choose class widths deliberately because wide classes can hide local structure.

A strong justification names both a benefit and a cost. For example, a histogram clearly compares distribution shape across many measurements, but exact readings cannot be recovered. Avoid selecting a chart only because it looks familiar.

sections.title: Choose for exact retrieval

prompt.text: Twenty-four integer scores must remain individually recoverable while showing their distribution. Choose a representation.

content.text: The dataset is small and numerical.
Exact values and ordering are required.
A stem-and-leaf diagram meets both needs.

sections.verification_note: Every leaf can be decoded with the key.

sections.title: Choose for a large continuous sample

prompt.text: Two thousand reaction times must be compared by shape, not by individual lookup.

content.text: The data are continuous and numerous.
Use a histogram with frequency density if widths differ.

sections.verification_note: The display scales well while making shape visible.

prompt.text: Use code 1 for dot plot and 2 for histogram. Which code suits 500 grouped continuous measurements?

feedback.text: A histogram communicates the shape of a large grouped continuous dataset.

blocks.text: Read the scale, key, class boundaries and units before calculating or interpreting.
Show the statistical definition or formula, calculate carefully, then explain what the result means for the displayed data.
